text: The composed SCR-02 page and the Excel file stay on the integration base (RWB-P2-E2033-APP) and read this service through RWB-P2-E2033-CON, while rwb-case also serves the same rows on its own base for the queue drill down and for any direct consumer; the duplicate serve is accepted as the stated cost of the split and the owner's rows are the single source of every value.
why: Arch v5 makes rwb-case the owner of the case, queue and timer rows, so the list cannot live only in a composed service, and the legacy story's operation is on the monolith base that the split divides between the two services, so one stated arrangement is needed.
read: RWB-E2-033 sections 4 and 12; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 4, 8 and 10; _work/msr/context/P3.md REST rows; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-01 and DP-13
confirm: Solution architect with the rwb-integration owner at the baseline review of RWB-P2-E2033-CON and in the wave 2 verification loop.
impact: If only the composed page is wanted, the two operations of 12.1 are removed and the story reduces to the export limit check; no acceptance criterion value changes, but section 7 and section 16 shrink to the limit assertion.

text: The row element names, the page envelope, the filter token list and the problem body of this base are proposed in section 12.1 and fixed by version 1 of RWB-P2-E2033-CON at its baseline review; MSG-GEN-006 takes the platform unavailable text of the platform message standard, and REQ-ACA-006 is read without its data-lake copy because the lake is removed under DP-17.
why: The legacy story fixes four response field names and no envelope or problem body, the platform unavailable message has no text in any source, and the requirement still names a removed lake, so one stated reading keeps the document testable without inventing values.
read: RWB-E2-033 sections 12 and 14; Recovery Workbench API Specification v4; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 37 (no data lake); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-17 row and R7.2 s12
confirm: Solution architect and the rwb-integration contract owner at the baseline review; the platform message standard owner for MSG-GEN-006.
impact: If the baseline fixes different names or a different envelope, section 12.1 and the row mapper change; no rule, no acceptance criterion value and no test case ID changes.

text: The page-size bounds and the extract row limit are parameter rows of rwb-case read with the version in force: the case-list page-size minimum 1 and maximum 200 as RWB-P3-E2011-APP serves them, and caselist.export.maxrows 10,000 as the legacy story assumed under DL11; the parameter and reference field IDs of section 11 are taken from the Logical Data Model at the baseline review.
why: The legacy story fixes the range 1 to 200 and the value 10,000 inside its flow and exception rows only, and the target forbids a business value in code, so the two limits need one stated home as data.
read: RWB-E2-033 sections 4 step 4, 5 X2, 5 X7, 8 BR7, 13 and 14; Recovery Workbench FSD P3 Case and workflow v4 A2.19 AC-EXC-P3-019-02; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-06 row
confirm: Solution architect with the rwb-case parameter owner and the queue-view story owner before the story's Done.
impact: If the bounds are owned by another service or the limit differs, one preconditions row and one parameter row change; the criteria keep their values and no test case ID changes.

text: ageDays keeps the meaning RWB-P3-E2011-APP gives it, the age in whole days since the entry date, and this story adds ageInStateDays for the legacy age in state from stage_clock_start with the entry date as the fallback; an unassigned case returns no owner value and is shown as the text Unassigned.
why: Legacy BR2 calls the stage-clock age ageDays while the queue-view story publishes ageDays as the entry-date age, and the legacy criteria read the unassigned owner as a text cell, so one stated reading prevents two services publishing one field name with two meanings.
read: RWB-E2-033 sections 7 AC1, 8 BR2 and 12; Recovery Workbench FSD P3 Case and workflow v4 A2.38 AC-P3-038-01; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 10
confirm: Solution architect with the queue-view story owner and the designer at the review of RWB-P2-E2033-CON.
impact: If the legacy name must be kept on ageDays, the two fields swap names in 12.1 and in the row mapper; the values, the rules and the test cases do not change.

text: This story adds no index and no migration: the legacy ix_timer_case_type on timer (case_id, timer_type) is covered by ix_timer_case_type_status on timer (case_id, timer_type, status) which RWB-P3-E2011-APP lands, and a second index on the same leading columns is not created.
why: Two indexes on the same leading columns of one table add write cost and no read, and the legacy story asked for its index before status existed in the filter, so one stated ruling keeps one index.
read: RWB-E2-033 section 13 (CREATE INDEX ix_timer_case_type); Recovery Workbench TSD P3 Case and workflow v3 (timer table); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-15 row
confirm: Solution architect with the ACE DB team at the review of the rwb_case Flyway sequence.
impact: If the separate index is required, one migration file is added to the rwb-case sequence; no query, no criterion and no test case changes.

text: The service connects with the rwb-case login of the service template, holding grants on rwb_case only, and keeps the legacy switch name rwb.casewf.case-list-ageing as a platform feature flag owned by the platform flag library; the login name and the flag mechanism follow the platform template and no source value is invented here.
why: The two names exist in the legacy story and in Arch v5 only as a schema, a login pattern and a flag name, and the story must not invent either, so both follow the platform template with the legacy flag name kept.
read: RWB-E2-033 sections 3 and 13; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 8 (19 rwb_* schemas, one login each); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-02 row and R3 default ruling on feature flags
confirm: DevOps lead and the platform flag owner at the deployment review of the rwb-case service.
impact: If the platform names the login or the flag differently, one values key and one wording change; no rule, no criterion and no test case changes.
